items.body_excerpt:
NRL Casualty Ward: Panthers' Yeo blow; Tupouniua sidelined again
Panthers skipper Isaah Yeo left the field in the first half at Go Media Stadium on Friday night with a suspected pectoral injury.
Yeo went in to make a tackle and immediately reached for his shoulder and had a shocked look on his face as he reeled away.
The NSW and Australian captain left the field in the 34th minute and cut a forlorn figure on the Panthers bench in the second term. He will be sent for scans to confirm the severity of the injury.
Before the game, Panthers centre Casey McLean had surgery on a fractured hand but is expected to miss only 1-2 matches.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The injury to McLean saw three-time premiership winner Izack Tago promoted to the starting side for Friday night's bumper clash with the Warriors.
In Friday's second game, Roosters fullback James Tedesco missed the Round 23 blockbuster against the Bulldogs after failing to overcome an ankle injury.
Tedesco sat out the second half of the Round 22 slaughter of the Cowboys with ice on his ankle but he was initially named to return against the Bulldogs.
The skipper dropped out of the side on Thursday and has been replaced by Cody Ramsey.
However, it was another blow for Bulldogs star back-rower Sitili Tupouniua who was back from a hamstring injury, but was ruled out in his return game - again with a hamstring injury.
"Not sure how bad it is, but he's felt it in the same spot where he injured about eight weeks ago, so not ideal," Bulldogs coach Cameron Ciraldo said after the game.
"He's pretty devastated because he was training really well and he was just excited to get back playing, this is what he does, this is what he loves doing, so he's pretty shattered."
The Knights suffered a blow ahead of Sunday's trip to Canberra with star centre Bradman Best dropping out with a calf strain suffered in last week's win over Brisbane.
Manly prop Ethan Bullemor suffered a head knock in training and will follow NRL concussion protocol. He will be stood down for 11 days meaning he will miss this week's clash against the Storm and next Friday's game against the Dolphins.
The Sea Eagles have also lost back-rower Kobe Hetherington for the remainder of the season after he suffered a ruptured bicep in training on Monday. He will undergo surgery next week.

Match Preview: Round 23 – Dolphins v Broncos
A Battle For Brisbane victory could be all the Dolphins need to secure their maiden finals berth.
And that’s what’s on the line when the Dolphins step out onto Suncorp Stadium on Saturday evening for another blockbuster clash with the Broncos.
A 13th win of the season will secure the Dolphins their first-ever finals appearance, adding even more significance to one of the biggest games on the calendar.
The last time the two sides met was earlier this season in Round 4, when the Broncos claimed a 26-12 victory. The Dolphins will be looking to turn the tables this time around as they chase a piece of club history.
Coming off a win over the Dragons in Wollongong last week, the Dolphins will look to carry that momentum into Saturday’s sold-out Battle for Brisbane.
There are also milestones on the line, with Jack Bostock set to make his 50th NRL and Dolphins appearance.
Jamayne Isaako is also closing in on a major club milestone, sitting on 975 points for the Dolphins and needing just 25 more to become the first player to reach 1,000 points for the club.
The winger has enjoyed a strong run at Suncorp Stadium, scoring nine tries in his past seven appearances at the venue.
Team News
Dolphins
Just one change has been made to the side that defeated the Dragons, with Sebastian Su’a joining the interchange in place of Ray Stone.
Kristian Woolf has otherwise retained the same starting 13 as the Dolphins look to secure their 13th victory of the season.
Broncos
Thomas Duffy moves into halfback in place of Adam Reynolds, who has been ruled out with concussion.
Xavier Willison will start at prop, with Va’a Semu moving to the bench, while Jaiyden Hunt and Billy Walters have been promoted to the starting side.
Jack Gosiewski also returns from a rib injury and has been named on the interchange.
Match-Up
Jack Bostock v Kotoni Staggs
The battle of the centres shapes as one to watch in Saturday’s Battle For Brisbane, with two New South Wales representatives lining up on opposite edges.
Bostock will make his 50th NRL and Dolphins appearance, and his 10th game of the season. Across his nine appearances this year, he has scored four tries, registered eight try assists, 22 tackle breaks and three line breaks.
On the opposite edge, Staggs will line up for his 162nd NRL game and 17th appearance of the season. The Broncos centre has crossed for eight tries this year, alongside two try assists, 61 tackle breaks and six line breaks.
Both centres bring plenty of power and attacking threat out wide, with their ability to break tackles and create opportunities for those around them making them key weapons for their respective sides.
With plenty on the line in Battle For Brisbane, whichever centre can make the bigger impact on their edge could prove crucial in deciding Saturday night’s contest.

Broncos aiming to create major disruptions in Dolphins derby
While the reality of no finals this year has sunk in, the Broncos are still hoping to play their part in shaping the finals race – starting with bringing down Brisbane rivals the Dolphins.
Kicking off week one of Indigenous Round with a bang, a sold-out crowd is expected at Suncorp Stadium for the latest instalment of the Battle for Brisbane, with Billy Walters saying his side still had plenty to play for to close out the season.
Billy Walters in action during his second NRL game back from an ACL injury against the Knights in Round 22. ©Zain Mohammed / NRL Images
“That's our goal for the rest of the year: to disturb a few of the teams still in the competition,” Walters said.
“The Dolphins are one; they're a team that's playing pretty well, and if we can put a dent in their road to trying to win the comp, then that's a win for us as well.”
With five games remaining in the season, coach Michael Maguire has shaken up his team for this week’s derby, while a head knock to skipper Adam Reynolds has forced his hand in the halves, bringing in Thomas Duffy to partner Ezra Mam.
In what could be a precursor to next season with Reynolds retiring from the NRL, Mam said he was looking forward to working on their combination on the field.
Ezra Mam and Tom Duffy first paired up in the halves in Duffy's Broncos debut in Round 6. ©Zain Mohammed / NRL Images
“Duffy's got a lot of great qualities that help my game as well” Mam said.
“We're pretty similar in age, so our chemistry and the way we move on the field is pretty intact.
“Having that free-flowing spine with my connection with Duffy and Walshy (fullback Reece Walsh) is going to be very exciting to go out there this weekend and put on the plays we've been doing for the last couple of weeks.
“We've played together a couple of times this year and we've had little moments where we've clicked.
“I feel like the more we can build on our combination throughout the back end of this year and hopefully into the pre-season and next year.
“With Duffy, he's got a really big organising game and I feel like he can organise the team as well and allow myself and Walshy to unlock our strike weapons."

For Mam, this round also holds an extra special meaning – on top of being able to play against a number of his former team-mates in the cross-town derby.
Sharing both Aboriginal and Torres Strait Island heritage, Mam said the two weeks of Indigenous Round were special and helped him showcase his culture.
“Indigenous Round is a big round for myself, I get to represent both sides of my heritage,” Mam said.
“For myself and the multiple players playing this round, they're very proud of who they are, where they are and where they're from.
“It's good that we can showcase that and provide a bit of education to the wider community about our culture."

The grandson of prominent Indigenous activists and grounded in his youth with culture, Mam continues to perform Torres Strait Island dances and strove to apply his cultural practices to his work on the football field.
"Last week I danced, so I still do it to this day,” Mam said.
“It's inside me and that's something I've been brought up with, thanks to my upbringing. It's something I've carried along the way.
“I feel like I show those traits on the footy field and around the club as well.
“I'm very grateful for my upbringing and my cultural side of things. It's good that I'm still connected with my culture.
“(But) I'm not where I want to be with my culture yet.
“I've still got a lot to learn and humble myself about, and that's always something I want to improve going forward."

Raiders v Knights: Sasagi returns; Frizell the milestone man
The Raiders will be looking to get back on track this week against the Knights after their recent run of good form was halted by Penrith.
Canberra were aiming for five wins in a row - but against this year's ladder leaders, they hit a snag and were unable to match them in their match at Mudgee.
They face a tough challenge this week however against a Knights side who are still full of belief, despite losing key players Dylan Brown and Dylan Lucas for the season.
Under coach Justin Holbrook this year, Newcastle's team have been rewarded for their spirit and will be looking to press their case for a top four finish with a win.
Last week they proved too strong for the Broncos and ended last year's defending premiers title defence.
In the absence of some of their stars, they have seen some new talents emerge, including forwards Cody Hopwood and Francis Manuleleua.

Storm v Sea Eagles: Munster back on deck; Laiafi to start
A new chapter is set to be written in one of the great rivalries of the modern era when Melbourne take on Manly on Saturday afternoon.
The teams will head across the Nullarbor to Perth's HBF Park for a crucial clash between two sides desperate to keep their finals hopes alive.
Manly are well-rested after last week's bye and eager to hit the ground running in their bid to climb back into the eight.
The Sea Eagles have lost four in a row but they have strike all across the park and can score points at will.
Defence will be a key area of focus, with Manly struggling in that aspect of the game in recent times.
Melbourne enter the clash battered and bruised after a tough few weeks that have seen Cam Munster, Harry Grant and Jahrome Hughes miss time with injuries.
The Storm currently sit 12th, six points outside the eight and they need to find form to keep a remarkable 15-year finals streak alive.

Bulldogs v Cowboys: Hopoate sidelined; Forwards shuffled
The round opens at Belmore Sports Ground with two sides keen to build momentum.
The Bulldogs enter the weekend after a big loss to the unbeaten Broncos, while the Cowboys arrive with renewed confidence after a hard-fought 18-16 win over the Raiders in Magic Round.
Canterbury have shown they are capable of competing physically, but consistency has been difficult to find. Their upset victory over the Sharks in Round 3 proved what they can achieve when they complete well and control possession.
North Queensland's season has ebbed and flowed, but their win over Canberra may prove a turning point. They defended strongly under pressure and found a way to secure two valuable competition points away from home.
The key battle could be through the middle third. The Cowboys forwards laid a strong platform last week, while Canterbury will need to dominate possession if they are to prevent North Queensland building pressure through repeat sets.
Belmore has always been a difficult venue for visiting teams, so watch this space.
